shieldLine.pattern: Aegis Vigil or its escorts occupy the physically dangerous side of the composition while the protected ship, station, transfer craft, or civilian group remains visibly behind or within the defensive geometry.
shieldLine.usage: Convoy defense, escort interception, debris screening, and scenes where protection must be visually legible without turning the ship into an abstract symbol.

rescueTransfer.pattern: Rescuers and civilians move through a clearly readable transfer path: damaged source, crossing point, receiving team, and safe destination all remain spatially intelligible.
rescueTransfer.usage: Docking-collar rescues, shuttle transfers, pressure-door crossings, tether work, and evacuations.

triageFlow.pattern: Medical and relief scenes preserve lanes for intake, stabilization, treatment, supplies, and movement onward; principal characters work inside the flow rather than posing apart from it.
triageFlow.usage: Mass-casualty response, refugee intake, medical overflow, and relief operations.

damageControl.pattern: Engineering teams cluster around the actual failing system, with routes to valves, breakers, braces, patch plates, extinguishers, pressure doors, or service trunks visible in the frame.
damageControl.usage: Shipboard failures where repair choices and physical access matter.

bridgeTriage.pattern: The bridge makes competing obligations visible at once: convoy contacts, distress calls, corridor limits, fuel state, damaged compartments, and escort positions remain readable around the command team.
bridgeTriage.usage: Command decisions in which protecting one asset changes the risk to another.
